docs.title: comfyui-apng-motion
docs.text:
ComfyUI 里做 能讲故事的 APNG / WebP / GIF：3–8 个关键帧 + latent 插值， 同一个工作流切 8 / 24 / 30 / 60 帧，SDXL 与 Moss/DiT 两套环境都有可导入的 JSON。

English · 简体中文

预览：60 帧 / 30fps / Moss-DiT 六拍故事《减肥破功》，配方是 assets/story.diet.json（prompt_mode: moss_zh）。 下面的联系表是按 segs 从成片抽出的真实关键拍。 网页主预览用 WebP q100（真彩、保住 60 帧；libwebp 在 q90 会把近重复帧并成 58 帧）；preview.gif 保留给聊天工具。 GIF 用全局固定调色板 + 关抖动重编码，避免 256 色量化造成的色块闪动。细节见格式对比。

docs.title: 它解决什么
docs.text:
错误做法 后果 batch_size=24 24 个独立噪声，播放必闪；固定 seed 也救不了 逐帧继承上一帧 动作顺了，但发色/瞳色会累积漂移 每帧都存图 输出目录被几百张 PNG 塞满

本项目的做法：首帧一次采样 → 关键帧全部从同一份首帧 latent 重绘 → N 个 latent 插值 → N 次解码 → 合并 → 三个成品文件。

docs.title: 三步
docs.text:
python scripts/detect_env.py
python scripts/doctor.py
python scripts/emit_workflow.py --base workflows/workflow-sdxl.json --story assets/story.4beat.json --out my.json

docs.title: 数据流
docs.text:
EmptyLatentImage(512,512,1)
        │
   KSampler K0   denoise 1.0, seed 123456789
        │  LATENT ─────────────────────────┐
        ├──────────────► CLIPTextEncode K1 ─┐
        ├──────────────► CLIPTextEncode K2 ─┤
        ├──────────────► CLIPTextEncode K3 ─┤
        │                                   │
   CLIPTextEncode「全局动作指导」──► ConditioningCombine（每帧一个）
                                          │
                     KSampler K1/K2/K3  positive 走合并后的条件
                     denoise 0.35-0.4，与 K0 同 seed、同首帧 latent
                                          │
        N × LatentInterpolate（N = frames，8–60；每帧一个 ratio；同一对 latent 内不重复）
                                          │
        N × VAEDecode ◄── VAE
                                          │
        ImageBatchMulti(inputcount=N)
                ├──► SaveAnimatedPNG   → output/APNG/final/apng/
                ├──► SaveAnimatedWEBP  → output/APNG/final/webp/
                └──► VHS_VideoCombine  → output/APNG/final/gif/

关键约束：

  1. 所有关键帧的 latent_image 都指向 K0 的 LATENT，不链式继承上一帧，否则颜色会累积漂移。 同时所有 KSampler 共用同一个 seed：seed 不同会带来不同噪声路径，插值时表现为色斑。
  2. 同一对 latent 上的 ratio 唯一。不同段（K0→K1 与 K1→K2）可以同值，样本对不同画面就不同；同一段里撞值才会被 Pillow 合并。
  3. 三个输出接同一个 batch，否则三种格式的帧序会不一致。

docs.title: 帧数不是写死的
docs.text:
--frames N（或剧情卡的 "frames": N）决定整条链的长度，--segs 之和必须等于 N：

  • 24 帧保留旧预设：3 拍 8/8/8、4 拍 6/7/6/5、5 拍 5/6/5/4/4；
  • 其它帧数按拍数平均分，余数给前几拍（30 帧 4 拍 → 8/8/7/7）；
  • ensure_frames() 会把 LatentInterpolate + VAEDecode 克隆到 N 个或删到 N 个， 再重建 ImageBatchMulti 的 image_1..image_N 与 widgets_values=[N]，并按 6 列重排画布位置。

校验口径也改了：不再硬编码 24，而是要求「插值数 = 解码数 = batch 接线数」，且 batch 的计数值必须等于实际接线数。

docs.title: 曲线
docs.text:
默认 linear：每段从 1.0 均匀降到 0.0，每帧步长恒定。

段1: 1.0 0.857 0.714 0.571 0.429 0.286 0.143 0.0
段2: 0.996 0.861 ... 0.004        （段首与上一段末几乎相接）
段3: 0.992 0.853 ... 0.008

ease 用 smootherstep，两端慢、中间快，单帧最大位移约为线性版的 1.9 倍； snap 是旧版幂曲线，前段几乎静止、末段猛冲，容易看成跳帧，只在对比时用。

段与段之间留 0.004 的微差，避免 Pillow 把相邻的完全同值帧合并。

docs.title: UI → API
docs.text:
--run 需要把 UI 工作流转成 API prompt。comfy_lib.ui_to_api 的做法：

  1. 用 /object_info/<type> 取节点的 required/optional 定义；
  2. 按 input_order 遍历，链接类型（MODEL/LATENT/...）走连线，其余取 widgets_values；
  3. 遇到 control_after_generate（如 KSampler 的 seed）多跳一格；
  4. 每个输入写成 [origin_node_id, origin_slot]。

docs.title: 为什么不用脚本逐帧生成
docs.text: 逐帧 img2img 需要每帧一次采样，N 帧就是 N 次采样；插值只需要 3–5 次采样 + N 次解码， 显存不变、耗时线性下降，而且中间帧由数学过渡，差异更均匀。 代价是没有真实运动轨迹，所以只适合微表演。

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
为什么不用 batch_size？ batch_size=N 是 N 个互相独立的噪声样本。固定 seed 只保证可复现，不会让它们变成连续帧。

为什么不像视频那样逐帧生成？ 逐帧 img2img 要 24 次采样，且会累积漂移（黑发漂成青蓝）。插值只需 3–5 次采样，中间帧由数学过渡。

为什么默认 24 帧？ 24 帧 @10fps = 2.4 秒，够放「起 → 转 → 收」。但帧数是预算不是规格：8 帧做轮播，12 帧做轻动作，24 帧是默认甜点，30 帧给五拍故事，60 帧给网页/Discord 的顺滑预览。都用 --frames 改。

为什么默认 10fps？ GIF 的延迟单位是 1/100 秒，10fps = 10cs 是精确值；12fps 会变成 8cs（12.5fps）。

为什么我的图动作很小？ 提高关键帧 denoise（xl 0.4 → 0.45，Moss 0.5 → 0.55），或加大 A/B 提示词差异。不要靠加帧数。

能让角色走起来吗？ 不能。这条路线没有真实轨迹。走位、转身要用 ControlNet 骨骼序列或视频模型（Wan / LTX）。

支持 Flux / SD1.5 / 别的模型吗？ 支持。emit_workflow.py 只认结构（1 个 denoise=1 的 KSampler + ≥2 个关键帧 + N 插值 + N 解码 + N 路合并 + 3 输出），模型名换成你自己的即可。

必须用 GPU 吗？ 出图需要。detect_env / doctor / emit_workflow / check_anim 都是 CPU 侧工具。

APNG 和 GIF 哪个好？ 见 APNG、GIF 与视频转 GIF。结论：聊天用 GIF，网页/透明用 WebP，文档/无损用 APNG。

为什么 GIF 比 APNG 还小？ GIF 是 256 色 + LZW，对平涂动漫非常友好；APNG 每帧整帧无损。

能商用吗？ 本仓库代码 MIT。模型与生成内容遵循模型许可与当地法律，与本仓库无关。

docs.title: APNG、GIF 与「视频转 GIF」：到底差在哪
docs.text: 这一页解释三件事：APNG 为什么适合做表情包、它和「拿视频转 GIF」有什么本质区别、 以及把 APNG 再转成 GIF 时会损失什么。

docs.title: 1 · APNG 是怎么存的
docs.text:
APNG 不是新格式，是 PNG 的扩展：在普通 PNG 里插入三类块。

块 作用 acTL 动画控制：num_frames（帧数）、num_plays（循环次数，0 = 无限） fcTL 每帧控制：宽高、偏移、delay_num / delay_den（该帧显示时长）、dispose_op、blend_op fdAT 第 2 帧及之后的图像数据

关键结论（APNG 规范原文）：

  • num_plays = 0 表示无限循环；num_frames 必须等于 fcTL 数量。
  • 帧时长 = delay_num / delay_den 秒；delay_den = 0 按 100 处理，即单位变成 1/100 秒。
  • 第 1 帧就是普通 PNG 的 IDAT，所以不支持 APNG 的解码器会退回显示一张静态 PNG——这是 APNG 最重要的使用逻辑：它天然向后兼容，不会出现"图裂了"。

这带来两个直接好处：

  1. 一个 .png 文件既是动图又是静态图，聊天软件预览、图床、CDN 都不会报错。
  2. 真彩色 + 真 alpha（RGBA），半透明边缘不糊。

代价是体积：APNG 的每一帧都是完整 PNG 数据，没有视频那种帧间预测（没有 P/B 帧、没有运动补偿）。 所以同样内容，APNG 通常比 GIF 大，更比 MP4/WebM 大一个量级。

备注：APNG 规范允许用 x_offset / y_offset + dispose_op 只更新帧的局部区域， 但 Pillow（ComfyUI 的 SaveAnimatedPNG 用的就是它）默认按整帧写，并且会把像素完全相同的相邻帧 合并、把时长累加到上一帧。这就是"排了 N 帧只导出更少帧"的根因（实测 24 帧导出 19 帧），也是本项目要求同一对 latent 上比例不重复的原因。

docs.title: 2 · 和「视频转 GIF」的本质区别
docs.text:
两条流水线完全不是一回事：

视频转 GIF：
  拍摄/生成视频 → H.264/H.265（帧间预测，YUV，有损）
      → 抽帧 → 调色板量化（≤256 色）→ GIF（LZW，1-bit 透明）

本项目（APNG 路线）：
  首帧采样 → 3–5 个关键帧（同一 latent 重绘）
      → LatentInterpolate 插出 N 帧（8–60，默认 24）→ VAE 解码（每帧都是完整 RGBA）
      → APNG / WebP / GIF 三路独立编码
维度 视频转 GIF 本项目 运动来源 真实采样，有运动模糊与物理轨迹 关键帧之间的数学插值，没有真实轨迹 能演什么 走位、转身、镜头运动、复杂交互 表情、呼吸、轻微头部动作；大动作要换 ControlNet / 视频模型 画质 受视频码率与量化影响 每帧独立高清，无压缩伪影 体积 视频本身很小，转 GIF 后暴涨 APNG 偏大，GIF 适中 可控性 需要重拍或重剪 改一句提示词即可换表演

一句话：视频转 GIF 是"记录已经发生的运动"，本项目是"在两个状态之间插值"。 前者适合真实动作，后者适合表情包式的微表演，而且可复现、可参数化。

docs.title: 3 · APNG 的特点（什么时候该用它）
docs.text:
特点 说明 向后兼容 不支持的软件显示第一帧，不会裂图 24 位真彩 + alpha 渐变、发丝、半透明光效都能保住 无损 DEFLATE 压缩，没有色带 浏览器支持 97.39% Chrome / Edge / Firefox / Safari / Android 全绿（caniuse，2026-11-23） 桌面查看器支持不一 Windows 自带照片不播 APNG；BandiView、浏览器可以 体积偏大 每帧整帧 PNG；512² × 24 帧约 4–7 MB，60 帧约 10–18 MB（随画面复杂度浮动） 无音频 纯图像序列

适合：网页 / 文档 / Discord（保留 alpha）、本地高清回看、需要"静态图兜底"的场景。

docs.title: 4 · APNG 转 GIF 会发生什么
docs.text: APNG → GIF 不是换壳，是降维编码。四件事一定发生：

docs.title: 4.1 颜色：24 位 → 8 位调色板
docs.text:
GIF 每帧最多 256 色。两种做法：

做法 结果 逐帧各自量化 帧与帧之间调色板跳变，播放时颜色"呼吸"、闪烁 全片统一调色板 不闪，但整片只能用 256 色，渐变与肤色容易出色带

本项目的 GIF 走 VHS 的 image/gif：palettegen 一次 + paletteuse 统一套用， 抖动算法 sierra2_4a。所以不闪，但色带和抖动噪点是必然的。

docs.title: 4.2 透明：真 alpha → 1-bit 透明
docs.text: APNG 的半透明（比如发梢、光晕）在 GIF 里只能全透明或全不透明， 边缘会出现硬边或白边。要透明素材，优先 WebP 或 APNG。

docs.title: 4.3 时间：毫秒级 → 1/100 秒
docs.text:
GIF 的帧延迟单位是 1/100 秒（GIF89a 的 GCE），所以实际帧率只能落在 100/n：

目标 fps GIF 实际延迟 实际 fps 10 10cs 10.00 12 8cs 12.50 9 11cs 9.09 8 12cs 8.33

另外多数浏览器对过短延迟有下限钳制，所以做表情包 8–12fps 就够，再高既看不出来也不准。

docs.title: 4.4 体积：不一定变大
docs.text:
直觉上 GIF 更差所以更大，实际常常相反——因为 GIF 的 LZW + 256 色对平涂动漫非常友好。 本项目实测（512²，ComfyUI 直出）：

环境 / 内容 帧数 APNG GIF WebP（lossless） SDXL / 银发校服 24 6.61 MB 2.41 MB 0.80 MB Moss / 银发校服 24 4.15 MB 2.72 MB 2.88 MB Moss / 雨夜霓虹 60 17.23 MB 7.21 MB 12.76 MB

同内容下体积近似线性（60 帧 ≈ 24 帧的 2.5 倍）；跨内容不可直接比，雨夜霓虹的单帧细节多，24 帧也会更大。

结论：GIF 通常比无损 APNG 小，但 WebP 开 lossless 时不一定比 GIF 小；要小就关掉 lossless、quality 80–90。

docs.title: 4.5 还有两个细节
docs.text:
• 相同帧会被合并：Pillow 写 APNG 时，像素完全相同的相邻帧会被丢弃并把 duration 累加到上一帧； GIF 侧不同编码器行为不一致，所以同一对 latent 上的比例不能重复（不同段之间同值是安全的）。
  • 循环次数：APNG num_plays=0、GIF 的 NETSCAPE2.0 扩展 loop=0，都是无限循环，语义一致。

docs.title: 4.6 网页预览：为什么最终用 WebP
docs.text:
仓库里的 docs/assets/preview.webp 是主预览，preview.gif 只做兼容备份。

文件 尺寸 帧数 体积 相邻帧差（avg） 旧 GIF（VHS 直出，512，sierra2_4a） 512×512 24 3.45 MB 2.49 新 GIF（全局调色板 + dither=none） 384×384 60 2.13 MB 1.94 新 WebP（quality 100，保住 60 帧） 384×384 60 1.46 MB 1.82

当前预览是 60 帧 / 30fps / Moss-DiT 的六拍故事《减肥破功》，配方 assets/story.diet.json。 画面细节比旧的 4 拍版本多，GIF 从 1.46 MB 涨到 2.13 MB；WebP 反而更小，所以网页主预览用 WebP。

WebP 的帧数有个坑：libwebp 的动画编码器会把「压缩后几乎一样」的相邻帧合并。 质量 90 时 60 帧会变成 58 帧（时长不变，但元数据不是 60）；质量 100 能保住 60 帧， 代价是体积从约 0.6 MB 涨到 1.8 MB。make_preview.py 默认用 100，并在保存后核对帧数， 对不上就回退 lossless。

GIF 只有 256 色。VHS 默认用 palettegen + paletteuse，抖动算法 sierra2_4a： 每一帧单独量化，调色板随帧变化，误差扩散的颗粒也在变。播放时人眼看到的就是「色块在闪」， 它和画面本身有没有动是两件事。

scripts/make_preview.py 的做法：

  1. 所有帧共用首帧的 256 色调色板；
  2. dither=Image.NONE，不做误差扩散；
  3. 缩到 384×384，颗粒更细、体积更小。

单帧量化误差均值仍在 2.3/255 左右，但帧与帧之间的量化噪声变一致，所以不再有闪烁感。

docs.title: 5 · 色块闪动的两个来源
docs.text:
排查顺序：先看 APNG，再看 GIF。

来源 怎么认 怎么修 生成端：关键帧 denoise 过高 APNG 相邻帧 diff 平均 > 2，脸上/衣服出现补丁状色斑 关键帧 denoise 降到 0.35–0.40；同 seed；同首帧 latent 生成端：曲线不均 diff 序列中段突然出现 4–5 的尖峰 --curve linear；别用 snap 编码端：GIF 调色板逐帧变化 APNG 干净，GIF 播放有块状噪点 固定全局调色板 + 关抖动；或改用 WebP 循环边界 最后一帧到第一帧 diff 特别大 让末拍回到首拍姿势

实测同一套内容：denoise 0.55 时 APNG diff 2.34、drift 8+；降到 0.35 后 diff 1.08、drift 2.63。 GIF 重编码后再降约 0.05。

想看这条路线和 Live2D、逐帧 AI、视频生成的定位差异与算力账，见 动图合成方案对比。

docs.title: 6 · 选型建议
docs.text: 场景 用哪个 理由 微信 / QQ 聊天、自定义表情 GIF 兼容性最好，体积可控 网页、Discord、需要透明 WebP 体积小、支持 alpha 文档、需要"静态兜底"、无损 APNG 不支持时显示第一帧，不裂图 需要真实动作（走位、转身） 视频模型 → MP4/WebM 本条路线做不了

docs.text:

docs.title: 1 · 作为 skill 安装
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/Gg22333/comfyui-apng-motion.git
cd comfyui-apng-motion
python scripts/install.py

install.py 会读取 skill.json 里的目标，装到：

  • ~/.codex/skills/comfyui-apng-motion
  • ~/.config/magpie/library/skills/comfyui-apng-motion（父目录存在时）

python scripts/install.py --dest /path/to/skills/comfyui-apng-motion

升级：重新跑一次。旧 SKILL.md 自动备份成 .bak-<时间戳>。

docs.title: 表情包动作库：怎么把「一个动作」写成可合成的关键帧
docs.text:
这一页解决的是内容问题，不是代码问题：同一条流水线，为什么有的片像表情包，有的片像卡住的 PPT。

结论先给：表情包不是「小视频」，是一个 1–3 秒、首尾能接上的微表演。 它只需要 2–4 个关键姿势，靠预备动作和停顿把动作读出来，不靠帧数堆。

docs.title: 1 · 平台规范决定了动作长度
docs.text:
做之前先看发给谁。三家主流平台的实际验收线：

平台 格式与尺寸 时长 / 帧数 体积 硬性要求 Telegram 动态贴纸 TGS（Lottie）512×512 ≤ 3 秒，60fps — 必须循环 Telegram 视频贴纸 WebM 512×512 ≤ 3 秒，≤ 30fps — 建议循环 LINE 动态贴纸 APNG .png 5–20 帧，≤ 4 秒，1–4 次循环 ≤ 1 MB/张 第一帧是商店封面；相同帧会被合并 微信表情 GIF 240×240 单张 ≤ 3 秒（按平台当期规范） ≤ 500 KB/张 一套 16 或 24 张 Discord / 网页 APNG / WebP 无硬限制 建议 ≤ 2 MB 首帧兜底、透明优先 WebP

来源见文末。两个直接推论：

  1. 8–24 帧就够。LINE 上限只有 20 帧；微信 240² 的 GIF 再高帧数也看不出来。 本项目默认 24 帧 @10fps = 2.4 秒，正好落在 Telegram 的 3 秒线内。
  2. 60 帧不是给聊天软件用的，是给网页、Discord、GitHub 预览、后续转 WebM 用的。 Telegram 的 60fps 指的是 TGS 矢量动画，不是 60 张位图；位图 60 帧只会让体积翻 2.5 倍。

帧数怎么选、各帧数的体积与算力账，见 用法 的「帧数怎么选」和 格式对比。

docs.title: 2 · 五拍语法：表情包的动作都是同一个骨架
docs.text:
把 actions 想成舞台提示，不是画面描述。一个能循环的动作只有五拍：

拍 作用 提示词里写什么 常见错误 K0 静息 循环接点，也是聊天列表封面 中性表情、正对镜头、嘴闭 一上来就是大笑，循环回 K0 会「变脸」 K1 预备 反方向蓄力，告诉观众要动了 吸气、挑眉、手抬起一半 直接跳到主动作，看起来像瞬移 K2 主动作 全片最大变化，剪影必须变 张嘴、后仰、手举到最高 同时改脸、手、身体、背景，插值必糊 K3 余震 过冲后回落，给动作重量 头回正、手放下、笑收一半 直接切回 K0，动作像被剪断 回到 K0 最后一段自动插回第一帧 不用写 曲线设成 snap，末帧冲太快

工作流里的对应关系：

K0 ──段1──► K1 ──段2──► K2 ──段3──► K3 ──段4──► K0

beats=4 就是 4 个关键帧、4 段，最后一段自动插回 K0（emit_workflow.py 的 dst = chain[(seg+1) % len(chain)]）。 所以 K0 必须是一个能收尾的姿势，不然循环接点会跳。

docs.title: 2.1 四拍怎么分配帧
docs.text:
frames=24 的默认分配：

拍数 segs 节奏感觉 3 8 / 8 / 8 起 → 一个动作 → 回落，最稳 4 6 / 7 / 6 / 5 起 → 预备 → 爆发 → 收，推荐 5 5 / 6 / 5 / 4 / 4 有剧情，但 24 帧会赶，建议加到 30/60

规律：预备短、爆发长、收尾中等。上面 shock 用 5/6/7/6，就是让惊吓来得快、停顿留得久。

docs.title: 3 · 提示词怎么写
docs.text:
一条关键帧提示由三段拼成，顺序固定：

lock（不变） + action（这一拍变什么） + style（画风，放最后）

emit_workflow.py 的 compile_prompt() 就是这么拼的。三个理由：

  1. lock 放最前：脸、发型、服装、构图锚死，插值才不会换人。
  2. action 放中间：只写这一拍变化的部分，不要重复 lock 里已有的内容。
  3. style 放最后：Moss 的文本编码器对末尾 token 权重最高，风格词放末尾才压得住动作词。

docs.title: 3.1 每拍只改一件事
docs.text:
想让人物… 写 不要写 笑 big smile, eyes half closed laughing, jumping, waving, background changes 惊讶 eyes wide, mouth slightly open turning around, camera zoom 生气 frowning, cheeks puffed whole body shaking, red background 打招呼 raising right hand, palm open walking toward viewer

最多同时改两个部位（例如「眼 + 嘴」或「手 + 眉」）。改三样以上，中间帧就会互相打架，出现重影和色斑。

docs.title: 3.2 全局动作指导写什么
docs.text:
motion（工作流里的「全局动作指导」）不是第二个动作，是全片共享的约束：

same camera, same framing, stable lighting, no zoom, no camera move

可以加：subtle head motion、rain falling、steam rising、warm morning light。 不要写：camera pans、zoom in、character walks——插值处理不了镜头运动，只会把画面拉花。

留空也可以。留空时工作流会旁路 ConditioningCombine，不稀释每帧提示（1.3.0 起）。

docs.title: 3.3 negative 只写会坏事的词
docs.text: 默认 negative 已经包含：photo, photorealistic, 3d render, collage, grid, multiple girls, different outfit, camera move, zoom, color shift。 不要往里堆 ugly, bad，那会连正常表情一起压掉。

docs.title: 4 · 动作库（17 组，直接调用）
docs.text: assets/motion-presets.json 是随包的动作库。每组都带：拍数、帧数、段数、fps、denoise、四条动作、全局指导、场景提示。

docs.title: 4.1 情绪类
docs.text: id 名称 节拍 适用 laugh 大笑 忍笑 → 爆发 → 后仰 → 收 聊天里表示笑到不行 cry 大哭 委屈 → 泪涌 → 抽泣 → 擦眼 求安慰、装可怜 shock 震惊 平静 → 瞳孔缩 → 后仰 → 僵住 听到离谱消息 angry 生气 皱眉 → 鼓脸 → 握拳 → 别头 假装生气 smug 得意 挑眉 → 斜眼 → 抱臂 → 轻笑 「我早就说了」 sigh 无语 半睁眼 → 呼气 → 垂肩 → 死鱼眼 冷场、无奈 panic 慌张 呆住 → 左右看 → 抱头 → 强笑 翻车现场 sleepy 困 哈欠 → 打盹 → 惊醒 早八、加班 love 比心 害羞 → 抬手 → 比心 → 收 表白、撒娇

docs.title: 4.2 动作类
docs.text: id 名称 节拍 适用 wave 打招呼 抬手 → 挥两下 → 收回 开场、打招呼 nod 点头 微笑 → 点头 → 再点 → 定住 同意、收到 shake 摇头 叹气 → 摇头 → 再摇 → 无奈 拒绝、不行 thumbsup 点赞 抬手 → 竖拇指 → 眨眼 → 收 认可、加油 think 思考 抬头 → 摸下巴 → 灵光 → 点头 「让我想想」

docs.title: 4.3 五拍小故事
docs.text:
id 名称 节拍 适用 rainy-walk 雨天出门 看雨 → 撑伞 → 踩水 → 回头 60 帧 / 30fps 的完整场景 morning-coffee 早八续命 趴桌 → 找咖啡 → 喝 → 满血 → 起身 五拍情绪曲线

故事类不要求「一个表情」，它演的是状态变化：困 → 清醒、平静 → 惊喜。 但结构不变：每一拍仍然只推进一步，最后一拍仍然插回 K0。

docs.title: 4.3.1 六拍全身故事（moss_zh）
docs.text:
diet-betrayal｜减肥破功｜60 帧 / 30fps / 640×640｜prompt_mode: moss_zh

拍 帧 动作 K0 0 坐直、叉腰、抬下巴、面前是沙拉碗 K1 10 背塌、双肘撑桌、头低到碗口、嘴角拉直 K2 22 身体右倾、右手撑桌、左手够地上的手机、屏幕冷光打脸 K3 26 缩肩、从桌下抱起炸鸡桶、鼓腮、额角一滴汗 K4 38 后靠椅背、举炸鸡到嘴边、眼睛闭成两道弯 K5 48 坐直、推走空桶、抱回沙拉碗、握拳（明天再减） 
python scripts/make_story.py --preset diet-betrayal --out assets/story.diet.json

这一组的关键约束：

  • 下半身全程固定在矮桌后面。腿的位置一变，latent 插值就会出现「双重腿」残影。
  • denoise 0.85–0.90。MOSS 是 8 步 DMD 蒸馏模型，低于 0.8 几乎不动（实测整片相邻帧差 0.03）。
  • motion 留空。写「不要推镜头 / 不要换角度」这类否定句，模型会理解成「保持原样」， 把本帧动作一起压掉。
  • 提示词用中文散文，每段以「。」结尾；prompt_mode 设成 moss_zh。

docs.title: 4.4 动作词汇表（直接粘进 actions）
docs.text:
热门表情包的动作高度套路化，翻来覆去就是下面这些。用法：每拍取「1 个动作短语 + 1 个表情短语」， 不要整句照抄，也不要一拍拍全用。

类别 可直接用的英文短语 问候 / 告别 wave hello · salute · bow · peace sign · blowing a kiss · goodbye wave 肯定 / 同意 nod · thumbs up · OK sign · clapping · fist pump · arms crossed with a nod 否定 / 拒绝 shake head · palm out · cross arms · turn away · shrug · push away 情绪爆发 laughing hard · crying · screaming · gasping · jaw dropped · rage · pouting · sulking 日常状态 yawning · sleepy · eating · drinking · working · studying · gaming · scrolling phone 亲密 / 撒娇 heart hands · hug · headpat · blushing · shy look · wink · leaning on shoulder 搞笑 / 梗 facepalm · sweat drop · anger vein · blank stare · side-eye · smirk · dizzy swirls 节奏 / 身体 bounce · sway · tilt head · lean back · lean forward · recoil · freeze · tremble

三条硬规则：

  1. 表情包的动作是符号，不是解剖。写 sweat drop、anger vein、blank stare 比写「眉头下压 3 毫米」有效。
  2. 一个 beat 只取一个动作短语。waving, jumping, winking 三条一起写，插值只会糊。
  3. 动作词放 action，镜头词放 motion。close-up、from above 不属于动作，写了会换构图。

docs.title: 5 · 用法
docs.text:
列出全部动作：

python scripts/make_story.py --list

用动作库生成剧情卡，再交给 emit_workflow.py：

python scripts/make_story.py \
  --preset laugh \
  --lock "masterpiece, best quality, 1girl, solo, upper body, silver hair, blue eyes, school uniform, simple background" \
  --name my-laugh \
  --out assets/story.my-laugh.json

python scripts/emit_workflow.py \
  --base workflows/workflow-sdxl.json \
  --story assets/story.my-laugh.json \
  --out my-laugh.json \
  --run

改帧数 / 帧率 / 段数：

# 12 帧轻量版（LINE 风格）
python scripts/make_story.py --preset wave --lock "..." --frames 12 --fps 12 --out story.wave12.json

# 五拍故事拉到 60 帧
python scripts/make_story.py --preset rainy-walk --lock "..." --frames 60 --fps 30 --out story.rain60.json

# 手动分配段数（必须满足 sum(segs) == frames）
python scripts/make_story.py --preset shock --lock "..." --frames 24 --segs 4,6,8,6 --out story.shock.json

make_story.py 会校验：

  • frames >= beats；
  • segs 段数 = 拍数；
  • sum(segs) == frames；
  • 每拍动作数与拍数一致。

场景类动作（rainy-walk、morning-coffee）会自动把 lock_hint 追加到 lock 后面；不想要就加 --no-hint。

docs.title: 6 · 按平台改参数
docs.text:
目标 frames fps 额外动作 Telegram 动态贴纸 24–60 30（导出后转 TGS/WebM） 512×512，≤3 秒 LINE 动态贴纸 8–20 8–10 缩到 370×320 内，压到 ≤1 MB 微信表情 24 10 缩到 240×240，GIF ≤500 KB Discord / 网页 24–60 15–30 优先 WebP，透明背景 GitHub 预览 24–60 15–30 384²，见 make_preview.py

体积换算：60 帧约为 24 帧的 2.5 倍；WebP q90 约为 APNG 的 1/7。详见 格式对比。

docs.title: 7 · 七个常见错误
docs.text: 症状 原因 修法 循环接点「变脸」 K0 不是静息姿势，或末拍没回 K0 actions[0] 写中性；用四拍模板 中间帧重影 / 色斑 一拍里改了三个以上部位 每拍只改 1–2 个部位；denoise 降到 0.4 手部糊成一团 手部大幅动作 + 低帧数 手部动作给 0.5 denoise；裁到上半身 画面被拉花 motion 里写了 camera move / zoom 只写 same camera, same framing 风格被动作词吃掉 style 写在 action 前面 固定顺序 lock + action + style 排了 24 帧只剩 19 帧 同一对 latent 上 ratio 重复 用 make_curve.py，别手填重复值 GIF 有色块闪 逐帧调色板 + 抖动 用 make_preview.py 的全局调色板 + dither=NONE

docs.title: 成品落盘：三个文件，一条路径
docs.text:
这一页只讲一件事：Queue 一次之后，文件应该出现在哪、为什么有时会出现在错的地方、怎么查、怎么清。

配套脚本：scripts/check_output.py（结构检查 + 可选归档）。

docs.title: 1 · 正确的目录长什么样
docs.text:
输出根目录永远在 ComfyUI 自己的 output/ 下，不在仓库里，也不在 skill 目录里：

<ComfyUI>/output/
└─ APNG/
   ├─ final/
   │  ├─ apng/anim24_00001_.png      ← 成品 APNG（无损，首帧可当静态图）
   │  ├─ webp/anim24_00001_.webp     ← 成品 WebP（可透明，体积最小）
   │  └─ gif/anim24_00001.gif        ← 成品 GIF（聊天用）
   │     └─ anim24_00001.png         ← VHS 首帧预览，插件副产物，可删
   └─ archive/
      ├─ frames/                     ← 需要留档的单帧（默认不产生）
      ├─ tests/                      ← 调参期试片
      └─ stray-<时间戳>/             ← check_output --fix 归档的游离文件

一次成功的 Queue 只产生 三个成品。gif/ 里那张同名 .png 是 VHS 自己写的首帧预览，不是第四份成品，也不代表"每帧落盘"又回来了。

<ComfyUI> 是 profile 里的 comfy_root。两套环境各有自己的 output：

profile output 根 profiles/xl.json D:\ComfyUI-aki-v3.2-xl\ComfyUI\output profiles/dit.json D:\ComfyUI-aki-v3.2-DiT\ComfyUI\output

换机器后路径由 detect_env.py 重新生成，不要照抄本文的盘符。

docs.title: 2 · 三个保存节点的硬规则
docs.text:
规则 说明 同一个 batch SaveAnimatedPNG、SaveAnimatedWEBP、VHS_VideoCombine 的 images 必须接在同一个 ImageBatchMulti 的输出上。各接各的 batch，三种格式的帧序会不一致。 不接单帧保存 工作流里不出现 SaveImage、PreviewImage。它们是"每帧落盘"和目录塞满的来源。 前缀带目录 filename_prefix 里的 / 会直接建子目录：APNG/final/apng/anim24。 前缀三路分开 三个节点分别写 .../apng/anim24、.../webp/anim24、.../gif/anim24，不能三路同前缀，否则互相覆盖。 改完刷新 改 filename_prefix 后必须 F5 刷新浏览器页面再 Queue。前端会缓存旧节点值，旧 prefix 就是这样把成品写回 output/APNG/ 根目录的。 fps 三路一致 三路都填同一个值；只改一路会出现 APNG/WebP/GIF 时长不一致。 不用固定文件名 ComfyUI 总会在前缀后追加 _00001_ 计数器。想要稳定名字就固定前缀，接受计数器；不要去手动改成品名，否则 check_output.py 会把它标成 odd_name。

节点参数（与 SKILL.md 第 3 节一致）：

节点 关键参数 推荐值 SaveAnimatedPNG filename_prefix / fps / compress_level APNG/final/apng/anim24 / 10 / 4 SaveAnimatedWEBP filename_prefix / fps / lossless / quality APNG/final/webp/anim24 / 10 / True / 90 VHS_VideoCombine frame_rate / loop_count / filename_prefix / format 10 / 0 / APNG/final/gif/anim24 / image/gif

docs.title: 3 · 文件为什么会跑到 output/APNG/ 根目录
docs.text:
本机确实出现过一次：output/APNG/anim24_00001_.png 直接躺在 APNG/ 下，既不在 final/apng/，也没有同批的 WebP/GIF。原因不是保存节点写错，而是运行时用的前缀是旧值。

四种常见来源：

来源 现象 处理 浏览器缓存旧 prefix 成品落 output/APNG/anim24_00001_.png 三个保存节点逐个确认前缀 → F5 → 重跑 跑了旧工作流 同一目录出现旧命名（anim_base_*、anim24_1_*） 用 workflows/workflow-*.json 或 emit_workflow.py 重新生成 历史 SaveImage output/ 根目录出现 anim_base_00001_.png 删掉保存节点；文件归档，不再当成品 旧脚本中间帧 anim24_1_00002_.png 这种带 _1_ 的 历史脚本产物，移到 archive/frames/

判断标准很简单：成品必须三件同批存在。缺 WebP 或 GIF 的那张 PNG，只是半次运行或旧前缀的残留。

docs.title: 4 · 检查与清理
docs.text:
# 只检查（默认 dry-run，不动文件）
python scripts/check_output.py --profile profiles/xl.json

# 把 APNG 根目录 / output 根目录的游离文件移进 archive/stray-<时间戳>/
python scripts/check_output.py --profile profiles/xl.json --fix

# 机器可读
python scripts/check_output.py --profile profiles/xl.json --json

退出码：0 无 FAIL，1 有 FAIL，2 路径不存在。

检查项：

级别 含义 FAIL stray_root output/APNG/ 根目录有文件 → 前缀旧值 / 前端没刷新 FAIL incomplete 某一批只有 1–2 种格式 → 保存节点没接同一 batch，或某路报错 WARN outside_apng output/ 根目录有 anim* 残留 → 历史 SaveImage 或旧前缀 WARN odd_name 文件名不符合 <name>_<5位>.<ext> → 手动改名或固定名 INFO vhs_sidecar gif 目录的同名 .png，VHS 首帧预览，可删 INFO archive 留档文件数量，不参与判定

手工清理（先看再动）：

$apng = 'D:\ComfyUI-aki-v3.2-xl\ComfyUI\output\APNG'
Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $apng -File | Select-Object Name, Length, LastWriteTime
# 确认是游离成品后，用脚本归档，不要直接删
python scripts/check_output.py --profile profiles/xl.json --fix

docs.title: 5 · 一次运行后的验收清单
docs.text:
1. output/APNG/ 根目录没有文件。
  2. final/apng、final/webp、final/gif 三处出现同一序号的三件成品。
  3. gif/ 里的同名 .png 是首帧预览，保留或删除都不影响动图。

docs.title: 动图合成方案对比：APNG、GIF、Live2D 与视频生成
docs.text:
这一页回答三个问题：

  1. APNG 到底是什么，和 GIF 差在哪。
  2. 本项目的「关键帧 + latent 插值」和 Live2D / Spine、逐帧 AI、视频生成分别是什么关系。
  3. 为什么这条路线在算力上明显更省。

docs.title: 1 · 先给结论
docs.text:
方案 生成方式 可交互 运行时依赖 相对成本 适合 本项目 3–5 个关键帧 → latent 插值 → N 帧（8–60，默认 24）→ APNG/WebP/GIF 否 无，浏览器/聊天软件直接播 低：K 次采样 + N 次解码 表情包、微表演、文档插图 逐帧 AI 24 次独立 img2img 否 无 高：24 次采样 每帧都要精确控制 batch_size=24 一次采样出 24 个独立噪声 否 无 中，但必闪 不推荐 视频生成 → GIF 视频模型出 MP4/WebM，再抽帧量化 否 无（成品） 很高：时序模型 + 转码 走位、转身、真实动作 Live2D / Spine 分层原画 + 网格绑定 + 参数曲线，运行时变形 是 需要 SDK / 播放器 美术与绑定成本高，运行时可交互 VTuber、游戏立绘、可互动角色 手绘序列帧 画师逐帧画 否 无 人力成本最高 高预算动画 Lottie / Rive 矢量关键帧 + 运行时插值 是 需要运行时 文件极小，但不适合写实/厚涂 UI 动效、矢量插画

一句话：Live2D 是「让人物活起来并接受输入」，本项目是「把一个微表演烘焙成一张到处能播的图」。

docs.title: 2 · APNG 的定义
docs.text:
APNG 不是新格式，是 PNG 的扩展。普通 PNG 里插入三类块就变成动画：

块 作用 acTL 动画控制：帧数 num_frames、循环次数 num_plays（0 = 无限） fcTL 每帧控制：宽高、偏移、delay_num / delay_den、dispose_op、blend_op fdAT 第 2 帧及之后的图像数据，带 4 字节序列号

规范里的几个硬事实（Mozilla APNG Specification）：

  • acTL 必须出现在第一个 IDAT 之前，才会被识别为 APNG。
  • 第一帧就是普通 PNG 的 IDAT，叫 default image；不支持 APNG 的解码器会显示这张静态图，而不是裂图。
  • 帧时长 = delay_num / delay_den 秒；delay_den = 0 按 100 处理，也就是单位变成 1/100 秒。
  • num_plays = 0 表示无限循环。
  • fcTL / fdAT 共用递增序列号，用来检测丢帧或顺序错误。

MDN 对 APNG 的定位写得很直接：

"Good choice for lossless animation sequences (GIF is less performant). AVIF and WebP have better performance but less broad browser support."

也就是说：APNG 是无损动画序列的稳妥选择；要更小用 WebP/AVIF，要最大兼容用 GIF。

docs.title: APNG 与 GIF 的核心差异
docs.text:
维度 APNG GIF 颜色 24 位真彩 + 真 alpha 每帧 ≤256 色调色板，1-bit 透明 压缩 DEFLATE，无损 LZW，有损量化 帧延迟 毫秒级（delay_num/delay_den） 1/100 秒（GIF89a GCE） 静态兜底 第一帧就是普通 PNG 第一帧就是普通 GIF 兼容性 浏览器广泛支持；Windows 照片不播 几乎所有平台都播 体积 每帧整帧 PNG，偏大 平涂动漫常常更小 透明边缘 半透明平滑 硬边/白边

详细的块结构、GIF 的 256 色与 1/100 秒限制、APNG→GIF 的四类损耗，见 APNG、GIF 与视频转 GIF。

docs.title: 3 · 和 Live2D / Spine 的区别
docs.text:
Live2D 的官方定位（Wikipedia 条目转述）：由 Live2D Ltd. 开发的专有 2D 动画库，用分层 2D 贴图建立绑定模型（rigged model），通过 tween / warp 产生 2.5D 运动；通过 SDK 集成进软件，Cubism 是绑定与制作工具。它常用于视觉小说、抽卡手游和 VTube Studio 这类面捕场景。

维度 Live2D / Spine 本项目 输入 分层 PSD/原画 + 网格 + 参数曲线 3–5 条提示词 + 一张剧情卡 制作 需要绑定师，逐部件调权重 不需要绑定，改提示词即可 运行时 需要 SDK / 引擎 / 播放器实时变形 无，成品图直接播 交互 可以眨眼、跟随、口型、面捕 不能，帧是烘焙死的 动作范围 关节级、可组合、可循环 关键帧之间的插值，只有微表演 输出 模型 + 贴图（不是一张图） 一个 APNG / WebP / GIF 文件 成本 美术 + 绑定 + 集成 一次 Queue，几秒到几十秒 适合 VTuber、游戏立绘、可互动角色 表情包、贴图、文档演示

边界要讲清楚：本项目做不出 Live2D 的实时互动，也做不出真正的关节运动。它省掉的是「绑定 + 运行时」，换来的是「一张图到处能播」。

docs.title: 4 · 和其他动图路线的区别
4.1 逐帧 AI（24 次采样）
docs.text:
每一帧都跑一次 img2img。动作最自由，但：

  • 采样次数 = 24；
  • 帧间没有共享 latent，发色/瞳色/线宽会累积漂移；
  • 需要额外的帧间约束（ControlNet、光流、参考图）才不闪。

docs.title: 4.2 batch_size=24
docs.text: 一次采样出 24 个互相独立的噪声样本。固定 seed 只保证可复现，不会让它们变成连续帧，播放必闪。它不是动画方案，只是批量出图。

docs.title: 4.3 视频生成 → GIF
docs.text:
先用 AnimateDiff / SVD / Wan / LTX 之类出视频，再抽帧、量化成 GIF。

  • 优点是真实运动、镜头运动、复杂交互；
  • 缺点是时序模型本身很重，生成成本远高于 3–5 次采样；
  • 转 GIF 还要再过一遍 256 色量化，颜色和透明都会掉。

docs.title: 4.4 手绘序列帧 / sprite sheet
docs.text: 画师逐帧画，质量上限最高，成本也最高；sprite sheet 还需要播放器按格子切帧，不是「一张图直接播」。

docs.title: 4.5 Lottie / Rive
docs.text: 矢量关键帧 + 运行时插值，文件极小、可交互，但表现的是矢量图形；厚涂、光影、发丝这类栅格细节不适合。

docs.title: 5.1 采样次数
docs.text:
ComfyUI 的 KSampler 在 denoise < 1 时并不是「只跑 denoise × steps 步」。源码 comfy/samplers.py 的 set_steps() 会先算 new_steps = int(steps / denoise)，再取最后 steps + 1 个 sigma，所以每个 KSampler 仍然执行 steps 次模型评估；denoise 改变的是起始噪声位置，不是迭代次数。

因此，按 steps=20 计算：

路线 采样次数 相对 24 帧逐帧（基准 480） 本项目 3 拍 3 × 20 = 60 少 87.5% 本项目 4 拍 4 × 20 = 80 少 83.3% 本项目 5 拍 5 × 20 = 100 少 79.2% 24 帧逐帧 24 × 20 = 480 基准

插值本身是 N 次 latent 线性混合，不调用模型；解码仍然是 N 次（这一点和逐帧路线相同，省不掉）。 关键点：帧数从 24 加到 60，采样次数不变（只跟拍数有关），涨的只有解码次数和体积。

docs.title: 5.2 显存与内存
docs.text:
SDXL 512×512 的 latent 是 64×64×4：

  • 单个 latent fp16 ≈ 32 KB，24 个 ≈ 768 KB，60 个 ≈ 1.9 MB；
  • 解码后的 24 张 512×512 RGBA ≈ 25 MB，60 张 ≈ 63 MB；
  • 插值节点只持有 latent，不持有解码图。

也就是说，这条路线增加的是几十 MB 级的图像缓冲，不是几 GB 的模型或视频缓存。真正的开销仍然是一次模型加载和 K 次采样。

docs.title: 5.3 文件体积（本机实测，512²）
docs.text:
环境 / 内容 帧数 APNG GIF WebP（lossless） SDXL / 银发校服 24 6.61 MB 2.41 MB 0.80 MB Moss / 银发校服 24 4.15 MB 2.72 MB 2.88 MB Moss / 雨夜霓虹 60 17.23 MB 7.21 MB 12.76 MB

GIF 常常比无损 APNG 小，是因为 LZW + 256 色对平涂动漫非常友好；要更小就把 WebP 的 lossless 关掉，quality 80–90。

docs.title: 5.4 什么时候不省
docs.text:
• 你要真实走位、转身、镜头运动：插值做不了，只能上视频模型或 ControlNet 序列，这时本方案不适用。
  • 你要实时互动、面捕、口型：用 Live2D / Spine，本方案不适用。
  • 你每帧都要精确构图：逐帧路线更直接，省不了。

docs.title: 6 · 选型建议
docs.text: 需求 选哪个 聊天表情包、贴图、文档动图 本项目 → GIF / WebP / APNG 网页、需要透明、体积敏感 本项目 → WebP 文档、需要静态兜底、无损 本项目 → APNG VTuber、可互动立绘、面捕 Live2D / Spine 真实动作、镜头运动 视频模型 → MP4/WebM（必要时再转 GIF） UI 动效、矢量插画 Lottie / Rive

docs.title: 剧情卡
docs.text:
一个 JSON 描述整段表演，emit_workflow.py 把它编译成关键帧提示词。

{
  "name": "anim24-4beat",
  "beats": 4,
  "frames": 24,
  "segs": [6, 7, 6, 5],
  "fps": 10,
  "denoise": 0.4,
  "lock": "masterpiece, best quality, 1girl, solo, upper body, looking at viewer, simple background",
  "style": "anime screencap, clean lineart, flat cel shading",
  "negative": "worst quality, low quality, blurry, watermark, text, signature",
  "actions": [
    "neutral expression, mouth closed, head straight",
    "eyes widened, eyebrows raised, head tilted 8 degrees",
    "eyes half closed, mouth open, head tilted back 12 degrees",
    "flat expression, eyes half lidded, mouth closed, head straight"
  ]
}

编译规则取决于 prompt_mode：

模式 编译结果 用在 tags（默认） lock, actions[i], style 英文逗号拼接 SDXL / 传统 CLIP moss_zh lock。\n action。\n style。 中文散文，换行分段 MOSS / Qwen-VL

tags 模式下 style 必须放最后：CLIP 对末尾 token 权重最高，画风写在中段会被动作词挤掉， 出图会掉进写实照相模式（表现为拼贴照、色块闪）。

moss_zh 模式下三段都写中文，每段以「。」结尾；不要混英文标签，也不要堆 masterpiece。

assets/story.diet.json 是完整范例：

python scripts/emit_workflow.py --base workflows/workflow-moss.json \
  --story assets/story.diet.json --size 640 --out diet60.json

docs.title: 帧数怎么选
docs.text:
帧数是参数，不是另一套工作流。--frames（或剧情卡的 "frames"）会把 LatentInterpolate / VAEDecode / ImageBatchMulti 三件套自动扩缩到 N 个。

帧数 fps 时长 适合 4 拍 segs 8 8 1.0 s 头像微动、聊天气泡 2,2,2,2 12 12 1.0 s 轻量贴纸 3,3,3,3 24 10 2.4 s 默认；表情循环 6,7,6,5 30 15 2.0 s 五拍故事、半身动作 8,8,7,7 60 30 2.0 s 网页/Discord 顺滑预览、五拍故事 15,15,15,15

--segs 之和必须等于 frames；不给 --segs 就按拍数平均分（余数给前几拍）。24 帧时保留旧预设 3 拍 8/8/8、4 拍 6/7/6/5、5 拍 5/6/5/4/4，其余帧数一律平均分。

python scripts/emit_workflow.py --base workflows/workflow-moss.json --story assets/story.preview.json \
  --frames 60 --segs 15,15,15,15 --fps 30 --out my-60f.json

docs.title: 生成工作流
docs.text:
python scripts/emit_workflow.py --base workflows/workflow-sdxl.json --story my-story.json --out my.json
拍数 段数分配（24 帧） 节点数（SDXL） 节点数（Moss） 3 8/8/8 67 69 4 6/7/6/5 70 72 5 5/6/5/4/4 73 75

节点数比早期版本多，是因为多了全局动作层：每个关键帧一个 ConditioningCombine， 加一个共享的 CLIPTextEncode 和两个 Note（参数清单 + 提示词写法）。全局动作留空时不建合并节点（空提示参与 ConditioningCombine 会稀释本帧提示，小模型直接掉画质），填了动作则每多一拍再加 1 个。 帧数只改插值 / 解码 / 合批三件的数量，不改拍数。

命令行直接给参数（不写 JSON）：

python scripts/emit_workflow.py --base workflows/workflow-sdxl.json \
  --beats 4 --segs 6,7,6,5 \
  --lock "masterpiece, 1girl, silver hair" --style "anime" \
  --actions "neutral|notice|react|settle" --out my.json

docs.title: 结构
docs.text:
K 个关键帧（KSampler，共用首帧 latent、同 seed）
  → N × LatentInterpolate
  → N × VAEDecode
  → ImageBatchMulti(N)
  → SaveAnimatedPNG + SaveAnimatedWEBP + VHS_VideoCombine(GIF)

N 就是总帧数。采样只做 K 次（每个关键帧一次），插值和解码是纯张量运算，所以帧数翻倍不等于算力翻倍。

docs.title: 提示词写法
docs.text:
SDXL（tags）

1girl, solo, full body, black short hair, blue eyes, beige hoodie,
dark shorts, barefoot, bedroom at night, warm lamp light,
〈这一拍动作〉,
anime screencap, clean lineart, flat cel shading

  • 画风放最后：CLIP 对末尾 token 权重最高。
  • 写画面不写效果：eyes wide, pupils small 而不是 shocked。
  • 负向单独一个 CLIPTextEncode。

MOSS（moss_zh）

一间温馨的小卧室，深夜。画面右侧有一盏暖色台灯，光从右前方斜照下来，落在木地板上。
固定机位，平视，全身镜头，人物从头到脚完整入画，双手和双脚都留在画框里。
小满：黑色短发，蓝色眼睛，身材微胖，穿着宽松的米色连帽卫衣和深色短裤，赤脚。
小满盘腿坐在矮桌前，背挺得很直，双手叉在腰上，抬起下巴，嘴角只上扬几毫米。
动漫赛璐璐风格，干净黑色线稿，平涂上色，暖色调，柔和阴影。
  • 中文散文，换行分段，每段以「。」结尾。
  • 不堆 quality tag：masterpiece / best quality 对它是噪声。
  • 用可测量的身体描述：震惊 = 双眼睁大、瞳孔缩小、嘴张开。
  • 构图写死：固定机位、平视、全身镜头、从头到脚完整入画。
  • 负向用中文。

assets/story.diet.json 是一个完整的六拍 moss_zh 范例； python scripts/make_story.py --preset diet-betrayal --out my.json 可以直接生成它。

docs.title: comfyui-apng-motion
docs.text:
Story-shaped coherent APNG / WebP / GIF from 3–8 keyframes in ComfyUI — one graph, 8 / 24 / 30 / 60 frames, importable JSON for both SDXL and Moss/DiT.

Preview: the six-beat story Diet Betrayal, 60 frames at 30 fps, Moss/DiT — recipe in assets/story.diet.json (prompt_mode: moss_zh). The contact sheet below is sampled from the real output by --segs. The primary preview is WebP q100 (true colour, all 60 frames; libwebp merges near-duplicates at q90); preview.gif remains for chat apps. The GIF is re-encoded with one global palette and dithering off, so 256-colour quantisation no longer reads as flicker. See formats.

docs.title: What it fixes
docs.text:
Common approach Result batch_size=24 24 independent noise samples; playback flickers, a fixed seed does not help Frame-by-frame inheritance Motion is smooth, but hair and eye colour drift across frames Saving every frame The output folder fills with hundreds of PNGs

This project instead: sample the first frame once → redraw every keyframe from that same first latent → interpolate N latents → decode N times → merge → write three files.

docs.title: Data flow
docs.text:
EmptyLatentImage(512,512,1)
        │
   KSampler K0   denoise 1.0, seed 123456789
        │  LATENT ─────────────────────────┐
        ├──────────────► CLIPTextEncode K1 ─┐
        ├──────────────► CLIPTextEncode K2 ─┤
        ├──────────────► CLIPTextEncode K3 ─┤
        │                                   │
   CLIPTextEncode "global motion" ──► ConditioningCombine (one per keyframe)
                                          │
                     KSampler K1/K2/K3 take the merged conditioning
                     denoise 0.35-0.4, same seed and same first latent
                                          │
        N × LatentInterpolate (N = frames, 8–60; one ratio per frame; unique within a latent pair)
                                          │
        N × VAEDecode ◄── VAE
                                          │
        ImageBatchMulti(inputcount=N)
                ├──► SaveAnimatedPNG   → output/APNG/final/apng/
                ├──► SaveAnimatedWEBP  → output/APNG/final/webp/
                └──► VHS_VideoCombine  → output/APNG/final/gif/

Hard constraints:

  1. Every keyframe's latent_image points at K0's LATENT, never chained from the previous keyframe, or colour drifts cumulatively. All KSamplers also share one seed: different seeds bring different noise paths, which interpolation turns into blotches.
  2. Ratios within one latent pair are unique. Different segments may reuse a value because the pair of images differs; only a collision inside one segment makes Pillow merge frames.
  3. All three outputs read the same batch, otherwise frame order diverges.

docs.title: Frame count is not hard-coded
docs.text:
--frames N (or "frames": N in the story card) sets the chain length, and --segs must sum to N:

  • 24 frames keeps the legacy presets: 3 beats 8/8/8, 4 beats 6/7/6/5, 5 beats 5/6/5/4/4;
  • other counts are split evenly with the remainder on the first beats (30 frames / 4 beats → 8/8/7/7);
  • ensure_frames() clones or deletes LatentInterpolate + VAEDecode nodes to reach N, rebuilds ImageBatchMulti's image_1..image_N and widgets_values=[N], and re-lays the canvas in six columns.

Validation no longer hard-codes 24: it requires interpolation count = decode count = batch wiring count, and the batch counter must match the actual number of connected inputs.

docs.title: Curve
docs.text:
Default linear: every segment walks from 1.0 down to 0.0 with a constant per-frame step.

segment 1: 1.0 0.857 0.714 0.571 0.429 0.286 0.143 0.0
segment 2: 0.996 0.861 ... 0.004      (almost flush with the previous segment)
segment 3: 0.992 0.853 ... 0.008

ease uses smootherstep: slow at both ends, fast in the middle, with a per-frame peak about 1.9x the linear version. snap is the legacy power curve: nearly frozen at the start, a rush at the end, easily read as a jump. Segments keep a 0.004 gap so Pillow never merges identical frames.

docs.title: UI to API
docs.text:
--run converts a UI workflow into an API prompt. comfy_lib.ui_to_api:

  1. fetches required/optional definitions via /object_info/<type>;
  2. walks input_order, wiring link inputs (MODEL/LATENT/...) and reading the rest from widgets_values;
  3. skips one extra slot for control_after_generate (for example KSampler's seed);
  4. writes each input as [origin_node_id, origin_slot].

docs.title: Why not generate every frame with a script
docs.text: Frame-by-frame img2img needs one sample per frame: N samples for N frames. Interpolation needs 3–5 samples plus N decodes; VRAM is unchanged and time grows linearly, while in-between frames come from a mathematical transition and are more evenly spaced. The trade-off is no real motion trajectory, which is why this route is for micro-performance only.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Why not batch_size? batch_size=N is N independent noise samples. A fixed seed makes them reproducible, not continuous.

Why not generate every frame like a video? Frame-by-frame img2img needs 24 samples and accumulates drift (black hair turning cyan). Interpolation needs 3–5 samples; in-between frames come from a mathematical transition.

Why 24 frames by default? 24 frames at 10 fps is 2.4 s, enough for "start → turn → settle". Frame count is a budget, not a spec: 8 for a flipbook, 12 for small motion, 24 as the default sweet spot, 30 for five-beat stories, 60 for smooth web/Discord previews. Change it with --frames.

Why 10 fps by default? GIF delay is in 1/100 s; 10 fps = 10cs exactly. 12 fps becomes 8cs (12.5 fps).

Why is the motion so small? Raise keyframe denoise (xl 0.4 → 0.45, Moss 0.5 → 0.55) or increase the difference between A/B prompts. Do not add frames.

Can the character walk? No. This route has no real trajectory. Walking and turning need a ControlNet pose sequence or a video model (Wan / LTX).

Does it support Flux / SD1.5 / other models? Yes. emit_workflow.py only cares about structure (one denoise=1 KSampler + ≥2 keyframes + N interpolations + N decodes + an N-way merge + 3 outputs); swap the model names.

Is a GPU required? For rendering, yes. detect_env / doctor / emit_workflow / check_anim / check_output are CPU-side tools.

APNG or GIF? See APNG, GIF and video-to-GIF. Short version: GIF for chat, WebP for web/transparency, APNG for documents and lossless.

Why is GIF sometimes smaller than APNG? GIF is 256 colours plus LZW, which suits flat anime very well; APNG stores every frame losslessly.

Where do the files go? output/APNG/final/{apng,webp,gif}/. See Output layout.

Commercial use? The code is MIT. Models and generated content follow their own licences and local law.

docs.title: APNG vs GIF vs video-to-GIF
docs.text: This page explains three things: why APNG suits sticker-style animations, how it differs from "turn a video into a GIF", and what is lost when an APNG is re-encoded as a GIF.

docs.title: 1 · How APNG is stored
docs.text:
APNG is not a new format; it is an extension of PNG that inserts three chunk types into an ordinary PNG.

Chunk Purpose acTL Animation control: num_frames, num_plays (0 = infinite) fcTL Per-frame control: size, offset, delay_num / delay_den, dispose_op, blend_op fdAT Image data for frame 2 and later

Key points from the specification:

  • num_plays = 0 means loop forever; num_frames must equal the number of fcTL chunks.
  • Frame duration = delay_num / delay_den seconds; delay_den = 0 is treated as 100, so the unit becomes 1/100 s.
  • Frame 1 is an ordinary PNG IDAT, so decoders without APNG support fall back to a static PNG. That is APNG's most important property: it degrades gracefully instead of showing a broken image.

Two direct benefits:

  1. One .png is both an animation and a still; chat previews, image hosts and CDNs do not break.
  2. True colour plus true alpha (RGBA); soft edges stay soft.

The cost is size: every APNG frame is a full PNG image, with no inter-frame prediction (no P/B frames, no motion compensation). For the same content, APNG is usually larger than GIF and an order of magnitude larger than MP4/WebM.

Note: the spec allows x_offset / y_offset plus dispose_op to update only part of a frame, but Pillow (what ComfyUI's SaveAnimatedPNG uses) writes full frames and merges adjacent pixel-identical frames, adding their duration to the previous frame. That is the root cause of "24 frames scheduled, 19 exported", and why this project forbids duplicate ratios within one latent pair.

docs.title: 2 · The real difference from video-to-GIF
docs.text:
Two completely different pipelines:

Video to GIF:
  capture/generate video → H.264/H.265 (inter-frame prediction, YUV, lossy)
      → frame extraction → palette quantization (≤256 colours) → GIF (LZW, 1-bit alpha)

This project (APNG route):
  first-frame sample → 3–5 keyframes (redrawn from the same latent)
      → LatentInterpolate to 24 frames → VAE decode (full RGBA per frame)
      → three independent encoders: APNG / WebP / GIF
Dimension Video to GIF This project Motion source Real sampling with motion blur and physical trajectories Mathematical interpolation between keyframes, no real trajectory What it can act Walking, turning, camera moves, complex interaction Expressions, breathing, small head moves; big motion needs ControlNet or a video model Quality Limited by video bitrate and quantization Every frame is full quality, no compression artifacts Size Video is small; the GIF explodes APNG is large, GIF moderate Control Reshoot or re-edit Change one prompt line to change the performance

In one sentence: video-to-GIF records motion that already happened; this project interpolates between two states. The former suits real action, the latter suits sticker-style micro-performance, and it is reproducible and parameterized.

docs.title: 3 · APNG characteristics
docs.text:
Characteristic Detail Backward compatible Unsupported software shows frame 1, not a broken image 24-bit colour + alpha Gradients, hair strands and translucent glows survive Lossless DEFLATE compression, no banding Browser support 97.39% Chrome / Edge / Firefox / Safari / Android all pass (caniuse, 2026-11-23) Desktop viewers vary Windows Photos does not play APNG; BandiView and browsers do Large Full PNG per frame; 512² × 24 frames is 4–7 MB, 60 frames is 10–18 MB depending on detail No audio Image sequence only

Good for: web pages, documents, Discord (alpha preserved), local high-quality review, anything that needs a still-image fallback.

docs.title: 4 · What APNG to GIF loses
docs.text: APNG to GIF is not a container swap; it is dimensionality reduction. Four things always happen.

docs.title: 4.1 Colour: 24-bit to an 8-bit palette
docs.text:
GIF allows at most 256 colours per frame. Two approaches:

Approach Result Per-frame quantization The palette jumps between frames; colours "breathe" and flicker One global palette No flicker, but the whole clip is limited to 256 colours; gradients and skin tones band

This project's GIF uses VHS image/gif: one palettegen pass plus paletteuse, with sierra2_4a dithering. No flicker, but banding and dither noise are unavoidable.

docs.title: 4.2 Alpha: true alpha to 1-bit transparency
docs.text: Semi-transparent regions (hair tips, glows) become either fully opaque or fully transparent, producing hard or white edges. For transparency, prefer WebP or APNG.

docs.title: 4.3 Time: milliseconds to 1/100 s
docs.text:
GIF frame delay is measured in 1/100 s (GIF89a GCE), so the real frame rate can only be 100/n:

Target fps GIF delay Actual fps 10 10cs 10.00 12 8cs 12.50 9 11cs 9.09 8 12cs 8.33

Browsers also clamp very short delays, so 8–12 fps is the practical range for stickers.

docs.title: 4.4 Size: not necessarily larger
docs.text:
GIF is worse in quality, so it feels like it should be bigger, but the opposite is common: LZW plus 256 colours is very kind to flat anime shading. Measured here (512², straight from ComfyUI):

Stack / content Frames APNG GIF WebP (lossless) SDXL / silver hair 24 6.61 MB 2.41 MB 0.80 MB Moss / silver hair 24 4.15 MB 2.72 MB 2.88 MB Moss / rainy neon 60 17.23 MB 7.21 MB 12.76 MB

Size is roughly linear for the same content (60 frames ≈ 2.5× of 24); across different content it is not comparable.

Conclusion: GIF is usually smaller than lossless APNG, but lossless WebP is not always smaller than GIF; for size, turn lossless off and use quality 80–90.

docs.title: 4.5 Two more details
docs.text:
• Identical frames get merged: when Pillow writes APNG, adjacent pixel-identical frames are dropped and their duration is added to the previous frame. GIF encoders differ, so ratios within one latent pair must be unique (equal values across different segments are safe).
  • Loop count: APNG num_plays=0 and the GIF NETSCAPE2.0 loop=0 both mean infinite, semantically identical.

docs.title: 4.6 Why the web preview is WebP
docs.text:
docs/assets/preview.webp is the primary preview; preview.gif is a compatibility copy.

File Size Frames Bytes Adjacent-frame diff (avg) Old GIF (VHS direct, 512, sierra2_4a) 512x512 24 3.45 MB 2.49 New GIF (global palette + dither=none) 384x384 60 2.13 MB 1.94 New WebP (quality 100, keeps all 60 frames) 384x384 60 1.46 MB 1.82

The current preview is 60 frames / 30 fps / Moss-DiT, recipe in assets/story.preview.json.

WebP has a frame-count trap: libwebp's animation encoder merges adjacent frames that are nearly identical after compression. At quality 90, 60 frames become 58 (same duration, wrong metadata); quality 100 keeps all 60, at the cost of growing from ~0.6 MB to 1.5 MB. make_preview.py defaults to 100 and verifies the frame count after saving, falling back to lossless if needed.

GIF has 256 colours. VHS runs palettegen + paletteuse per frame with sierra2_4a dithering: every frame gets its own palette and its own dither grain. On playback that reads as blocks flickering, independent of whether the artwork moves.

scripts/make_preview.py fixes it by sharing one palette across all frames, disabling dither, and downscaling to 384 px. The per-frame quantisation error stays around 2.3/255, but the error becomes consistent between frames, so the flicker disappears.

docs.title: 5 · Two sources of colour flicker
docs.text:
Check the APNG first, then the GIF.

Source How to recognise Fix Generation: keyframe denoise too high APNG adjacent diff avg > 2, patchy blotches on face/clothes drop keyframe denoise to 0.35-0.40; same seed; same first latent Generation: uneven curve diff series has 4-5 spikes in the middle --curve linear; avoid snap Encoding: per-frame GIF palette APNG clean, GIF shows blocky noise global palette + no dither; or use WebP Loop seam last frame to first frame diff is large bring the last beat back to the first pose

Measured on the same content: denoise 0.55 gave APNG diff 2.34 and drift 8+; 0.35 gives diff 1.08 and drift 2.63. Re-encoding the GIF removes another ~0.05.

For how this route compares with Live2D, frame-by-frame AI and video generation, including the compute bill, see Animation approaches compared.

docs.title: 6 · Which format to ship

docs.title: Motion library: turning one action into composable keyframes
docs.text:
This page is about content, not code: why the same pipeline produces a sticker in one run and a frozen slideshow in another.

Short answer: a sticker is not a tiny video. It is a 1–3 second micro-performance whose first and last pose connect. It needs 2–4 key poses, anticipation and a hold — not more frames.

docs.title: 1 · Platform specs decide the length
docs.text:
Check the destination before you render:

Platform Format and size Duration / frames Size cap Hard requirement Telegram animated sticker TGS (Lottie) 512×512 ≤ 3 s, 60 fps — must loop Telegram video sticker WebM 512×512 ≤ 3 s, ≤ 30 fps — loop recommended LINE animated sticker APNG .png 5–20 frames, ≤ 4 s, 1–4 loops ≤ 1 MB each frame 1 is the shop cover; identical frames get merged WeChat sticker GIF 240×240 ≤ 3 s per sticker ≤ 500 KB each sets of 16 or 24 Discord / web APNG / WebP no hard limit ≤ 2 MB recommended still-image fallback, alpha preferred

Sources at the end. Two consequences:

  1. 8–24 frames is enough. LINE caps at 20 frames; a 240² WeChat GIF gains nothing from more. The project default, 24 frames @10 fps = 2.4 s, sits inside Telegram's 3 s line.
  2. 60 frames is for the web, Discord, GitHub previews and later WebM export — not for chat stickers. Telegram's 60 fps refers to vector TGS, not 60 bitmap frames; 60 bitmaps only multiply file size by ~2.5.

Frame-count trade-offs and size/sampling math: Usage and Formats.

docs.title: 2 · The five-beat grammar
docs.text:
Treat actions as stage directions, not image descriptions. A loopable action has five beats:

Beat Role What to write Common mistake K0 rest loop seam and chat-list cover neutral face, facing viewer, mouth closed starting at peak laugh, so the loop "changes face" K1 anticipation wind-up in the opposite direction inhale, eyebrow lift, hand half raised jumping straight to the action; reads as a teleport K2 action largest change; silhouette must change mouth open, lean back, hand at peak changing face, hands, body and background at once K3 settle overshoot and fall back head recentres, hand lowers, smile softens cutting straight to K0; the action looks clipped back to K0 final segment interpolates home nothing to write using snap, so the last frames rush

Workflow mapping:

K0 ──seg1──► K1 ──seg2──► K2 ──seg3──► K3 ──seg4──► K0

beats=4 means 4 keyframes and 4 segments; the last segment wraps to K0 (dst = chain[(seg+1) % len(chain)]). So K0 must be a pose that can end the clip, or the seam jumps.

docs.title: 2.1 Segment budgets at 24 frames
docs.text:
Beats segs Feel 3 8 / 8 / 8 rest → one action → settle; safest 4 6 / 7 / 6 / 5 rest → wind-up → burst → settle; recommended 5 5 / 6 / 5 / 4 / 4 story-shaped, but crowded at 24; use 30/60

Rule: short anticipation, long burst, medium settle. shock uses 5/6/7/6 so the scare lands fast and holds.

docs.title: 3 · How to write the prompt
docs.text:
A keyframe prompt is assembled in a fixed order:

lock (constant) + action (what changes this beat) + style (look, last)

That is exactly what compile_prompt() does. Why:

  1. lock first pins face, hair, outfit and framing; interpolation cannot swap the character.
  2. action in the middle describes only the delta; do not repeat the lock.
  3. style last because Moss's text encoder weights trailing tokens most; style at the end survives action words.

docs.title: 3.1 Change one thing per beat
docs.text:
Goal Write Avoid laugh big smile, eyes half closed laughing, jumping, waving, background changes shock eyes wide, mouth slightly open turning around, camera zoom angry frowning, cheeks puffed whole body shaking, red background wave raising right hand, palm open walking toward viewer

At most two body parts per beat (eyes + mouth, or hand + brow). Three or more fight each other and produce ghosts and colour blotches in the in-betweens.

docs.title: 3.2 What goes into the global motion layer
docs.text:
motion (the "全局动作指导" node) is not a second action; it is a shared constraint:

same camera, same framing, stable lighting, no zoom, no camera move

You may add subtle head motion, rain falling, steam rising, warm morning light. Do not write camera pans, zoom in, character walks — interpolation cannot handle camera motion and will smear the frame.

Leaving it empty is fine: the workflow bypasses ConditioningCombine so the per-frame prompt is not diluted (since 1.3.0).

docs.title: 3.3 Keep negatives narrow
docs.text: The default negative already covers photo, photorealistic, 3d render, collage, grid, multiple girls, different outfit, camera move, zoom, color shift. Do not pile on ugly, bad; that suppresses ordinary expressions too.

docs.title: 4 · The library (17 presets)
docs.text: assets/motion-presets.json ships with the repo. Each preset carries beats, frames, segments, fps, denoise, four actions, a motion layer and a scene hint.

docs.title: 4.1 Emotions
docs.text: id Name Beats Use laugh Laugh hold back → burst → lean back → settle laughing hard cry Cry pout → tears → sob → wipe comfort me shock Shock calm → pupils shrink → lean back → freeze outrageous news angry Angry frown → puff cheeks → fists → turn away fake anger smug Smug brow raise → side-eye → arms crossed → chuckle "told you so" sigh Sigh half-lidded → exhale → shoulders drop → deadpan dead air panic Panic blank → look around → hands on cheeks → forced smile everything is on fire sleepy Sleepy yawn → doze → jolt awake early shift love Heart hands shy → raise hands → heart → hold affection

docs.text: id Name Beats Use wave Wave raise → wave → lower greeting nod Nod smile → nod → nod again → settle agreed shake Shake sigh → shake → shake again → resigned nope thumbsup Thumbs up raise → thumb → wink → lower approval think Think look up → chin → idea → nod let me think

docs.title: 4.3 Five-beat stories
docs.text:
id Name Beats Use rainy-walk Rainy walk notice rain → umbrella → puddle → look back 60 frames / 30 fps scene morning-coffee Morning coffee desk → find coffee → drink → refreshed → stand five-beat emotional curve

Stories are not "one expression"; they act out a state change: sleepy → awake, calm → delighted. The structure is unchanged: one step per beat, and the last segment still interpolates back to K0.

docs.title: 4.4 Action vocabulary (paste into actions)
docs.text:
Popular sticker packs reuse a small vocabulary. Use one action phrase + one expression phrase per beat; do not copy a whole list into every beat.

Category Ready-to-use phrases Greeting / farewell wave hello · salute · bow · peace sign · blowing a kiss · goodbye wave Yes / approval nod · thumbs up · OK sign · clapping · fist pump · arms crossed with a nod No / refusal shake head · palm out · cross arms · turn away · shrug · push away Emotional burst laughing hard · crying · screaming · gasping · jaw dropped · rage · pouting · sulking Daily state yawning · sleepy · eating · drinking · working · studying · gaming · scrolling phone Affection heart hands · hug · headpat · blushing · shy look · wink · leaning on shoulder Comedy / meme facepalm · sweat drop · anger vein · blank stare · side-eye · smirk · dizzy swirls Rhythm / body bounce · sway · tilt head · lean back · lean forward · recoil · freeze · tremble

Three hard rules:

  1. Sticker motion is symbolic, not anatomical. sweat drop, anger vein, blank stare work better than millimetre-level brow descriptions.
  2. One action phrase per beat. waving, jumping, winking together only produces mush after interpolation.
  3. Action words go in action; camera words go in motion. close-up and from above are framing changes, not actions.

docs.title: 5 · Usage
docs.text:
List presets:

python scripts/make_story.py --list

Build a story card, then hand it to emit_workflow.py:

python scripts/make_story.py \
  --preset laugh \
  --lock "masterpiece, best quality, 1girl, solo, upper body, silver hair, blue eyes, school uniform, simple background" \
  --name my-laugh \
  --out assets/story.my-laugh.json

python scripts/emit_workflow.py \
  --base workflows/workflow-sdxl.json \
  --story assets/story.my-laugh.json \
  --out my-laugh.json \
  --run

Override frames, fps or segment budgets:

python scripts/make_story.py --preset wave --lock "..." --frames 12 --fps 12 --out story.wave12.json
python scripts/make_story.py --preset rainy-walk --lock "..." --frames 60 --fps 30 --out story.rain60.json
python scripts/make_story.py --preset shock --lock "..." --frames 24 --segs 4,6,8,6 --out story.shock.json

make_story.py validates frames >= beats, len(segs) == beats, sum(segs) == frames, and that every preset has one action per beat. Scene presets append their lock_hint to your lock; pass --no-hint to suppress it.

docs.title: Output layout: three files, one path
docs.text:
This page covers one thing: where files should appear after one Queue, why they sometimes land in the wrong place, and how to check and clean up.

Companion script: scripts/check_output.py (structure check plus optional archiving).

docs.title: 1 · What the correct tree looks like
docs.text:
The output root is always ComfyUI's own output/, never the repository and never the skill directory:

<ComfyUI>/output/
└─ APNG/
   ├─ final/
   │  ├─ apng/anim24_00001_.png      ← APNG (lossless; first frame works as a still)
   │  ├─ webp/anim24_00001_.webp     ← WebP (alpha, smallest)
   │  └─ gif/anim24_00001.gif        ← GIF (chat)
   │     └─ anim24_00001.png         ← VHS first-frame preview, safe to delete
   └─ archive/
      ├─ frames/                     ← single frames kept on purpose (not produced by default)
      ├─ tests/                      ← tuning samples
      └─ stray-<timestamp>/             ← stray files archived by check_output --fix

One successful Queue produces three deliverables. The same-named .png inside gif/ is the first-frame preview written by VHS; it is not a fourth deliverable and does not mean per-frame saving is back.

<ComfyUI> is the comfy_root in your profile. Each install has its own output:

Profile Output root profiles/xl.json D:\ComfyUI-aki-v3.2-xl\ComfyUI\output profiles/dit.json D:\ComfyUI-aki-v3.2-DiT\ComfyUI\output

On another machine, regenerate paths with detect_env.py; do not copy the drive letters above.

docs.title: 2 · Hard rules for the three save nodes
docs.text:
Rule Why Same batch SaveAnimatedPNG, SaveAnimatedWEBP and VHS_VideoCombine must read from the same ImageBatchMulti output. Separate batches produce different frame orders. No single-frame savers Do not add SaveImage or PreviewImage. They are how per-frame dumps and full folders happen. Prefix carries the path A / in filename_prefix creates subdirectories: APNG/final/apng/anim24. Three different prefixes Use .../apng/anim24, .../webp/anim24, .../gif/anim24. Identical prefixes overwrite each other. Refresh after editing After changing filename_prefix, press F5 in the browser before Queue. The frontend caches old node values; a stale prefix is exactly how files end up in output/APNG/ root. Same fps everywhere All three nodes take the same value, otherwise durations diverge. Counters are normal ComfyUI always appends _00001_. Fix the stem, accept the counter. Renaming by hand makes check_output.py report odd_name.

Node parameters (same as SKILL.md §3):

Node Key parameters Recommended SaveAnimatedPNG filename_prefix / fps / compress_level APNG/final/apng/anim24 / 10 / 4 SaveAnimatedWEBP filename_prefix / fps / lossless / quality APNG/final/webp/anim24 / 10 / True / 90 VHS_VideoCombine frame_rate / loop_count / filename_prefix / format 10 / 0 / APNG/final/gif/anim24 / image/gif

docs.title: 3 · Why a file can land in output/APNG/ root
docs.text:
It happened on this machine once: output/APNG/anim24_00001_.png sat directly under APNG/, with no matching WebP or GIF. The save node was not misconfigured; the run used a stale prefix.

Four common sources:

Source Symptom Fix Cached prefix in the browser Artifact at output/APNG/anim24_00001_.png Confirm all three prefixes → F5 → rerun Old workflow Old names such as anim_base_*, anim24_1_* Regenerate from workflows/workflow-*.json or emit_workflow.py Historical SaveImage output/anim_base_00001_.png at the output root Remove the save node; archive the file Old script intermediate frames Names containing _1_, _2_ Historical frames; move to archive/frames/

The test is simple: a real deliverable exists as a set of three. A PNG without its WebP/GIF siblings is a half-finished run or a stale-prefix leftover.

docs.title: 4 · Check and clean
docs.text:
# Check only (dry run by default)
python scripts/check_output.py --profile profiles/xl.json

# Move strays from APNG root / output root into archive/stray-<timestamp>/
python scripts/check_output.py --profile profiles/xl.json --fix

# Machine-readable
python scripts/check_output.py --profile profiles/xl.json --json

Exit codes: 0 no FAIL, 1 has FAIL, 2 path missing.

Level Meaning FAIL stray_root Files directly under output/APNG/ → stale prefix or unrefreshed frontend FAIL incomplete A run has only one or two formats → outputs not on the same batch, or one node failed WARN outside_apng anim* leftovers at output/ root → historical SaveImage or old prefix WARN odd_name Name does not match <name>_<5 digits>.<ext> → manual rename or fixed stem INFO vhs_sidecar Same-named .png in gif/, VHS first-frame preview, safe to delete INFO archive Archive file count, not part of the verdict

Manual cleanup (look before touching):

$apng = 'D:\ComfyUI-aki-v3.2-xl\ComfyUI\output\APNG'
Get-ChildItem -LiteralPath $apng -File | Select-Object Name, Length, LastWriteTime
# Once confirmed as strays, archive with the script rather than deleting by hand
python scripts/check_output.py --profile profiles/xl.json --fix

docs.title: 5 · Acceptance checklist
docs.text:
1. output/APNG/ root contains no files.
  2. final/apng, final/webp, final/gif contain the same counter for the three formats.
  3. The same-named .png in gif/ is the first-frame preview; keeping or deleting it does not affect the animation.
  4. Run check_anim.py:
& '<ComfyUI-python>' scripts\check_anim.py `
  '<ComfyUI>\output\APNG\final\apng\anim24_00001_.png' --expect 24

Expected: frames=24, loop=0, identical_pairs=0, color_drift < 6.

  1. Run check_output.py again: FAIL 总数: 0.

docs.title: 6 · Archive conventions
docs.text:
Directory Contents Produced by final/ Three deliverables The three save nodes gif/*.png VHS first-frame preview VHS plugin archive/tests/ Tuning samples, comparison runs Manual archive/frames/ Single frames kept on purpose Manual (none by default) archive/stray-<timestamp>/ Strays and old-prefix leftovers check_output.py --fix

Do not keep workflow backups in ComfyUI/user/default/workflows/. A same-named -v1.json shows up as a second workflow in the UI; keep backups under archive/ and leave only the active file in the workflows directory.

docs.title: 7 · What must not land in the repo
docs.text:
The repo and the skill folder hold source and web assets only. Run outputs stay in ComfyUI's own output/:

Path Should contain Should not contain <ComfyUI>/output/APNG/final/ the three finals single-frame PNGs, stale prefixes repo docs/assets/ preview.webp / preview.gif / storyboard-*.webp raw APNG, _00001_ outputs repo root sources, docs, workflows/ any copy of output/ scratch dirs one-off scripts, test renders long-lived PNG / WebP

Only two scripts write into docs/assets/, and both write web assets, not finals:

  • make_preview.py → docs/assets/preview.{webp,gif}
  • make_storyboard.py → docs/assets/storyboard-<name>.webp

Check: git status should show no image changes other than those two files.

docs.title: Animation approaches compared: APNG, GIF, Live2D and video generation
docs.text:
This page answers three questions:

  1. What APNG actually is, and how it differs from GIF.
  2. How this project's "keyframes + latent interpolation" relates to Live2D / Spine, frame-by-frame AI and video generation.
  3. Why this route is significantly cheaper in compute.

docs.title: 1 · The short answer
docs.text:
Approach How it is made Interactive Runtime dependency Relative cost Best for This project 3–5 keyframes → latent interpolation → N frames (8–60, default 24) → APNG/WebP/GIF No None; browsers and chat apps play it Low: K samples + N decodes Stickers, micro-performance, docs Frame-by-frame AI 24 independent img2img runs No None High: 24 samples Per-frame precision batch_size=24 One sample, 24 independent noise images No None Medium, but always flickers Not recommended Video generation → GIF Video model → MP4/WebM → frame extraction/quantization No None (deliverable) Very high: temporal model + transcode Walking, turning, real motion Live2D / Spine Layered art + mesh rigging + parameter curves, deformed at runtime Yes Needs an SDK/player High art/rigging cost; interactive at runtime VTubers, game sprites, interactive characters Hand-drawn sequence An artist draws every frame No None Highest labour cost High-budget animation Lottie / Rive Vector keyframes + runtime interpolation Yes Needs a runtime Tiny files, unsuitable for painterly raster art UI motion, vector illustration

In one sentence: Live2D brings a character to life and accepts input; this project bakes one micro-performance into an image that plays anywhere.

docs.title: 2 · What APNG is
docs.text:
APNG is not a new format; it is an extension of PNG. Insert three chunk types into an ordinary PNG and it becomes an animation:

Chunk Purpose acTL Animation control: num_frames, num_plays (0 = infinite) fcTL Per-frame control: size, offset, delay_num / delay_den, dispose_op, blend_op fdAT Image data for frame 2 and later, with a 4-byte sequence number

Hard facts from the specification (Mozilla APNG Specification):

  • acTL must appear before the first IDAT for the file to be recognised as APNG.
  • Frame 1 is an ordinary PNG IDAT, the default image; decoders without APNG support show that still instead of a broken image.
  • Frame duration = delay_num / delay_den seconds; delay_den = 0 is treated as 100, so the unit becomes 1/100 s.
  • num_plays = 0 means loop forever.
  • fcTL / fdAT share increasing sequence numbers to detect dropped or reordered frames.

MDN states the positioning plainly:

"Good choice for lossless animation sequences (GIF is less performant). AVIF and WebP have better performance but less broad browser support."

In other words: APNG is the safe lossless animation sequence; use WebP/AVIF for size and GIF for maximum compatibility.

docs.title: APNG vs GIF
docs.text:
Dimension APNG GIF Colour 24-bit true colour + true alpha ≤256-colour palette per frame, 1-bit transparency Compression DEFLATE, lossless LZW, lossy quantization Frame delay Millisecond-level (delay_num/delay_den) 1/100 s (GIF89a GCE) Still fallback Frame 1 is an ordinary PNG Frame 1 is an ordinary GIF Compatibility Broad browser support; Windows Photos does not animate Plays almost everywhere Size Full PNG per frame, larger Often smaller for flat anime Alpha edges Smooth semi-transparency Hard or white edges

For the chunk layout, GIF's 256-colour and 1/100 s limits, and the four losses in APNG→GIF, see APNG, GIF and video-to-GIF.

docs.title: 3 · The difference from Live2D / Spine
docs.text:
Live2D's official positioning (as summarised by Wikipedia): a proprietary 2D animation library by Live2D Ltd. that builds rigged models from layered 2D textures, using tweening and warping to produce 2.5D motion; models integrate through an SDK, and Live2D Cubism is the authoring tool. It is common in visual novels, gacha games and facial-capture apps such as VTube Studio.

Dimension Live2D / Spine This project Input Layered PSD/art + mesh + parameter curves 3–5 prompts + one story card Authoring A rigger adjusts weights per part No rigging; edit a prompt Runtime SDK/engine/player deforms in real time None; the image plays directly Interactivity Blinks, gaze, lip-sync, face capture None; frames are baked Motion range Joint-level, composable, loopable Interpolation between keyframes; micro-performance only Output Model + textures (not a single image) One APNG / WebP / GIF file Cost Art + rigging + integration One Queue, seconds to tens of seconds Best for VTubers, game sprites, interactive characters Stickers, emotes, documentation

Be explicit about the boundary: this project cannot do Live2D's real-time interaction or true joint articulation. It removes rigging and runtime, and in exchange gives you one image that plays anywhere.

docs.title: 4 · The difference from other animation routes
4.1 Frame-by-frame AI (24 samples)
docs.text:
Run img2img once per frame. Maximum freedom, but:

  • 24 samples;
  • no shared latent, so hair colour, eye colour and line width drift cumulatively;
  • extra constraints (ControlNet, optical flow, reference images) are needed to stop flicker.

docs.title: 4.2 batch_size=24
docs.text: One sample produces 24 independent noise images. A fixed seed makes the run reproducible, not continuous; playback always flickers. It is batch image generation, not an animation method.

docs.title: 4.3 Video generation → GIF
docs.text:
Generate video with AnimateDiff / SVD / Wan / LTX, extract frames and quantize to GIF.

  • Pros: real motion, camera moves, complex interaction.
  • Cons: a temporal model is far heavier than 3–5 samples; GIF conversion adds a 256-colour quantization pass that loses colour and alpha.

docs.title: 4.4 Hand-drawn sequence / sprite sheet
docs.text: An artist draws every frame: the highest quality ceiling and the highest cost. A sprite sheet also needs a player to slice frames; it is not "one image that plays".

docs.title: 4.5 Lottie / Rive
docs.text: Vector keyframes plus runtime interpolation: tiny files and interactivity, but they describe vector shapes. Painterly shading, hair strands and soft light do not fit.

docs.title: 5 · The compute bill: where the saving comes from
5.1 Sampling passes
docs.text:
ComfyUI's KSampler does not run only denoise × steps iterations when denoise < 1. In comfy/samplers.py, set_steps() computes new_steps = int(steps / denoise) and then keeps the last steps + 1 sigmas, so every KSampler still performs steps model evaluations; denoise changes the starting sigma, not the iteration count.

With steps=20:

Route Sampling passes Versus 24-frame frame-by-frame (baseline 480) This project, 3 beats 3 × 20 = 60 87.5% fewer This project, 4 beats 4 × 20 = 80 83.3% fewer This project, 5 beats 5 × 20 = 100 79.2% fewer 24-frame frame-by-frame 24 × 20 = 480 baseline

Interpolation itself is N linear blends on latents and calls no model. Decoding is still N passes; that part is not saved. Key point: going from 24 to 60 frames does not add sampling passes (only beat count matters); only decode time and file size grow.

docs.title: 5.2 VRAM and memory
docs.text:
An SDXL 512×512 latent is 64×64×4:

  • one fp16 latent ≈ 32 KB; 24 ≈ 768 KB, 60 ≈ 1.9 MB;
  • 24 decoded 512×512 RGBA images ≈ 25 MB, 60 ≈ 63 MB;
  • interpolation nodes hold latents, not decoded images.

So the added footprint is tens of megabytes of image buffers, not gigabytes of model or video cache. The real cost remains one model load plus K sampling passes.

docs.title: 5.3 File size (measured here, 512²)
docs.text:
Stack / content Frames APNG GIF WebP (lossless) SDXL / silver hair 24 6.61 MB 2.41 MB 0.80 MB Moss / silver hair 24 4.15 MB 2.72 MB 2.88 MB Moss / rainy neon 60 17.23 MB 7.21 MB 12.76 MB

GIF is often smaller than lossless APNG because LZW plus 256 colours suits flat anime very well. For smaller files, turn off WebP lossless and use quality 80–90.

docs.title: 5.4 When it does not save
docs.text:
• Real walking, turning or camera moves: interpolation cannot do it; use a video model or a ControlNet sequence.
  • Real-time interaction, face capture, lip-sync: use Live2D / Spine.
  • Precise composition on every frame: frame-by-frame is more direct.

docs.title: 6 · Choosing a route
docs.text: Need Choose Chat stickers, emotes, documentation GIFs This project → GIF / WebP / APNG Web, transparency, size-sensitive This project → WebP Documents, still-image fallback, lossless This project → APNG VTubers, interactive sprites, face capture Live2D / Spine Real motion, camera moves Video model → MP4/WebM (convert to GIF only if needed) UI motion, vector illustration Lottie / Rive

docs.title: Story card
docs.text:
One JSON file describes the whole performance; emit_workflow.py compiles it into keyframe prompts.

{
  "name": "anim24-4beat",
  "beats": 4,
  "frames": 24,
  "segs": [6, 7, 6, 5],
  "fps": 10,
  "denoise": 0.4,
  "lock": "masterpiece, best quality, 1girl, solo, upper body, looking at viewer, simple background",
  "style": "anime screencap, clean lineart, flat cel shading",
  "negative": "worst quality, low quality, blurry, watermark, text, signature",
  "actions": [
    "neutral expression, mouth closed, head straight",
    "eyes widened, eyebrows raised, head tilted 8 degrees",
    "eyes half closed, mouth open, head tilted back 12 degrees",
    "flat expression, eyes half lidded, mouth closed, head straight"
  ]
}

Compile rule: keyframe_i = lock + actions[i] + style, fixed order, only the action changes.

style last is deliberate: Moss's LLM text encoder weights the tail tokens most, so anime screencap, clean lineart, flat cel shading placed mid-prompt gets buried by the action words and the render falls back to photographic mode (visible as collage frames and colour blotches).

docs.title: Choosing a frame count
docs.text:
Frame count is a parameter, not a second workflow. --frames (or "frames" in the story card) resizes LatentInterpolate / VAEDecode / ImageBatchMulti to N.

Frames fps Duration Best for 4-beat segs 8 8 1.0 s avatar twitch, chat reaction 2,2,2,2 12 12 1.0 s light sticker 3,3,3,3 24 10 2.4 s default; expression loop 6,7,6,5 30 15 2.0 s five-beat story, half-body action 8,8,7,7 60 30 2.0 s smooth web/Discord preview, five-beat story 15,15,15,15

--segs must sum to frames; omit it and the frames are split evenly across beats (remainder to the first beats). At 24 frames the classic presets stay: 3 beats 8/8/8, 4 beats 6/7/6/5, 5 beats 5/6/5/4/4.

python scripts/emit_workflow.py --base workflows/workflow-moss.json --story assets/story.preview.json \
  --frames 60 --segs 15,15,15,15 --fps 30 --out my-60f.json

docs.title: Generate a workflow
docs.text:
python scripts/emit_workflow.py --base workflows/workflow-sdxl.json --story my-story.json --out my.json
Beats Segment split (24 frames) Nodes (xl) Nodes (moss) 3 8/8/8 67 69 4 6/7/6/5 70 72 5 5/6/5/4/4 73 75

The node count grew with the global-motion layer: one ConditioningCombine per keyframe, plus one shared CLIPTextEncode and one Note.

Straight from the command line:

python scripts/emit_workflow.py --base workflows/workflow-sdxl.json   --beats 4 --segs 6,7,6,5   --lock "masterpiece, 1girl, silver hair" --style "anime"   --actions "neutral|notice|react|settle" --out my.json

--seed-mode same (default) pins every keyframe to the same seed. offset adds +1 per keyframe and reintroduces flicker.

docs.text:
Scope Node What it controls Whole clip CLIPTextEncode "global motion" action, camera, lighting, style; one edit affects every keyframe Per keyframe CLIPTextEncode "K0 / K1 / ..." expression, pose, gaze Per keyframe sampling each KSampler seed, steps, cfg, sampler, scheduler, denoise Pacing N x LatentInterpolate ratio easing curve; linear is the most even Speed three save nodes fps same value in all three; fps x frames = duration (24 @ 12 fps = 2 s) Prompt dialect --prompt-mode tags|moss_zh / story-card prompt_mode tags = English comma tags; moss_zh = Chinese prose Size latent width/height or --size 640 Moss 512 or 640; SDXL 512–1024 Naming filename_prefix apng/, webp/, gif/ Quality APNG compress_level, WebP lossless/quality, VHS loop/pingpong size and playback

From the CLI:

python scripts/emit_workflow.py --base workflows/workflow-sdxl.json --story my-story.json \
  --motion "slow head tilt, stable lighting" \
  --seed 777777 --denoise 0.35 --steps 24 --cfg 5.5 \
  --curve linear --out my.json

docs.title: Curve choice
docs.text: Value Behaviour When linear (default) constant per-frame step least visible stepping; best for stickers ease slow-fast-slow when you want anticipation and follow-through snap nearly frozen then a rush legacy behaviour, comparison only

docs.title: Switching models
docs.text:
The contract is loader-agnostic:

Family Loader nodes Keyframe denoise SD 1.5 CheckpointLoaderSimple 0.45-0.55 SDXL / Illustrious / NoobAI CheckpointLoaderSimple 0.35-0.45 FLUX.1 UNETLoader + DualCLIPLoader + VAELoader 0.45-0.55 Moss / DiT UNETLoader + CLIPLoader (type=moss_image) + VAELoader 0.50-0.55

Denoise values are field experience. On SDXL, above ~0.42 the keyframe redraw starts changing clothes and background, and latent interpolation turns that into colour blotches.

docs.title: Validate
docs.text:
python scripts/emit_workflow.py --validate my.json

Checks: link integrity, interpolation count = decode count = ImageBatchMulti links, unique ratios within one latent pair, three outputs on the same source, keyframes sharing one latent, no SaveImage.

docs.title: Run
docs.text:
UI: drag the JSON into ComfyUI and press Queue.

Headless:

python scripts/emit_workflow.py --validate my.json --run --profile profiles/xl.json

It submits the API prompt, polls, prints the artifact paths and runs check_anim.py automatically.

docs.title: Inspect the artifacts
docs.text:
python scripts/check_anim.py output/APNG/final/apng/anim60_00001_.png --expect 60

Watch four values: frames=N (matching --frames), loop=0, identical_pairs=0, and color_drift. Moss at denoise 0.5 measures around 18 and still looks fine; SDXL at 0.35 measures about 2.6. Above 20 means the keyframe redraw is changing too much.

docs.title: Where files land
docs.text: See Output layout. Short version: output/APNG/final/{apng,webp,gif}/, three files per run, plus one VHS first-frame preview PNG in gif/.

docs.title: Workflows
docs.text:
This page only covers dropping a JSON into ComfyUI. For story cards see usage, for per-beat tuning see motion library.

The source files live in workflows/. The download links below are mirrored into docs/assets/workflows/ by scripts/sync_workflows.py at build time.

docs.title: Download
docs.text:
Environment 3 beats 4 beats Notes SDXL workflow-sdxl.json workflow-sdxl-4beat.json CheckpointLoaderSimple, 20–30 steps, cfg 5–7 Moss / DiT workflow-moss.json workflow-moss-4beat.json UNETLoader + CLIPLoader + VAELoader, 8 steps, cfg 1.0 Preview — workflow-sdxl-preview.json Builds the repo preview; same seed, denoise 0.35

24 frames is the default. For 8 / 30 / 60 frames you do not switch files:

python scripts/emit_workflow.py --base workflows/workflow-moss.json \
    --story assets/story.diet.json --size 640 --out my-60.json

--frames rebuilds the interpolate / decode / batch triplet; nothing else is rewired.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
K keyframe KSamplers (shared first latent, shared seed)
  → N × LatentInterpolate
  → N × VAEDecode
  → ImageBatchMulti(N)
  → SaveAnimatedPNG + SaveAnimatedWEBP + VHS_VideoCombine(GIF)

N is the frame count. Sampling happens K times (once per keyframe); interpolation and decoding are plain tensor ops, so doubling frames does not double compute.

docs.title: Knobs on the canvas
docs.text:
Node What to change CLIPTextEncode "全局动作指导（所有关键帧共享）" Camera, lighting, framing, whole-clip motion. One edit applies to K0..Kn. Empty = bypass CLIPTextEncode "K0 首帧提示" / "K1 提示" / … What happens in this beat Every KSampler seed / steps / cfg / denoise / sampler / scheduler, per beat Note "可调参数清单" Cheat sheet written on the canvas Note "提示词写法（SDXL / MOSS 两套）" Two prompt dialects + frame table

Beat length follows the LatentInterpolate distribution: more interpolation nodes in a segment means a slower beat. emit_workflow.py --segs lays this out for you.

docs.title: Import
docs.text:
1. Open the matching ComfyUI instance.
  2. Drag the JSON onto the canvas.
  3. Point the loader at your local models:
  4. SDXL: CheckpointLoaderSimple
  5. Moss / DiT: UNETLoader + CLIPLoader (type=moss_image) + VAELoader
  6. Confirm the three save nodes use APNG/final/{apng,webp,gif}/....
  7. Press F5 before queueing, or the frontend may keep the old prefix.

docs.title: Environment differences
docs.text:
SDXL Moss / DiT VRAM from 6 GB from 8 GB (512 / 640 verified) steps 20–30 8 (DMD distilled, do not raise) cfg 5–7 1.0 keyframe denoise 0.35–0.45 0.50–0.80 text encoder CLIP (comma tags) Qwen-VL (Chinese prose) prompt mode tags moss_zh

Raising Moss steps to 20 or cfg to 6 only makes it muddier. SDXL is the opposite: below 20 steps or cfg below 5 it loses detail.

docs.title: Prompt dialects
docs.text:
SDXL (tags) — comma tags, subject first, style last, describe pixels not feelings:

1girl, solo, full body, black short hair, blue eyes, beige hoodie,
〈this beat〉,
anime screencap, clean lineart, flat cel shading

MOSS (moss_zh) — Chinese prose, one paragraph per idea, every paragraph ends with 「。」, no quality tags, framing stated explicitly:

一间温馨的小卧室，深夜。画面右侧有一盏暖色台灯，光从右前方斜照下来，落在木地板上。
固定机位，平视，全身镜头，人物从头到脚完整入画，双手和双脚都留在画框里。
小满：黑色短发，蓝色眼睛，身材微胖，穿着宽松的米色连帽卫衣和深色短裤，赤脚。
小满盘腿坐在矮桌前，背挺得很直，双手叉在腰上，抬起下巴，嘴角只上扬几毫米。
动漫赛璐璐风格，干净黑色线稿，平涂上色，暖色调，柔和阴影。

assets/story.diet.json is a complete six-beat moss_zh example; python scripts/make_story.py --preset diet-betrayal --out my.json regenerates it.
